items.text: The most common final expense mistake isn't the wrong policy type - it's the wrong amount. People often buy round numbers instead of adding up what a funeral, final medical bills, and small debts actually come to. Worth doing the math first.

The question we get wrong the least is whole life vs. term. The one we get wrong the most is the amount.

Final expense buyers tend to reach for a round number instead of adding up what it is actually meant to cover: funeral and burial or cremation costs, any final medical bills not covered by other insurance, and small debts that would otherwise land on family. Those numbers vary a lot by region and by the choices a family makes, and they are worth pricing out specifically rather than guessing.

The other side of the mistake is buying more than needed because a number sounded reassuring. Final expense policies are priced by the death benefit, so overbuying is a real, ongoing cost with no benefit attached to it.

The right process is to add up the real numbers first, then size the policy to that. It usually takes fifteen minutes and it changes the answer more often than people expect.

Honorbrook Insurance, Tysons VA. honorbrook-insurance.com
